findings.description: A live-format AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables and therefore committed to source control and stored in Terraform state. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or state file access can retrieve these long-lived static credentials; they should be replaced by the function's execution role or a Secrets Manager/SSM reference.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which hold secrets here) are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are returned in cleartext to any principal with configuration read permission. A customer-managed CMK would add a key-policy access-control boundary around the stored secrets.

The function pins runtime nodejs12.x, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled dependencies unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, making exfiltration of the embedded credentials trivial if the function code is compromised.

The assume role policy trusts the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the trust relationship is broader than the single intended function and provides no defence-in-depth against cross-account confused-deputy use.
